terra.problem: The text does not say they camped for the night.
The text does not say the people thought they were only arguing with Moses.
The text does not say how soon Moses cried out to the LORD.
Moses fears the people will stone him; the text does not say the crowd threatened to do it.
The text tells Moses to bring the staff, but does not say he needs it at the rock.
The text does not say striking the rock is why Moses brings the staff.
Calling the event a rock trick makes the water from the rock the joke.
The text does not say the name will last forever or that the argument was long.
The text does not say nobody is resting. The claim about thirsty people not resting also adds an unsupported detail.
Joshua obeys Moses, but the text does not say he did not argue or ask for a meeting.
“Wrong century” uses “wrong” in response to the baker's answer.
The text does not say everybody can see Moses from the hilltop.
The text does not say Moses does not have to say a word during the battle.
The text does not say when Aaron and Hur began holding Moses' hands, so it does not establish how long they held them.
The LORD commands Moses to write and recite the words; this passage does not say Moses did so.
The joke makes naming an altar the punchline. Holy things are not to be the joke.
Genesis 22:14 says Abraham named a place The LORD Will Provide, not an altar.
